paragraphs.text: Welcome back to another episode of Tis the Podcast that is determined to keep the spirit of Christmas alive 365 days a year. I'm Thom. I'm Anthony. And since we don't have Julia, I just cut her name by a third as well.

This is our first ever Julia Liss show. I know. It's our first ever, like just you and me on the main feed. I know. Me and her have done it once before without you on the main feed. That came out wrong. But you know what I meant, listeners.
So this is a milestone. I feel much more replaceable, though, than Julia. Julia, I mean, I would say if you ask listeners, we're both replaceable. She's the one who's not.
But she's at Disney World right now on a fabulous vacation. Good for her.
And here we are.
But hey, next month she'll be jealous when you're on a fabulous trip to New York City and get to see your favorite elf.
Just FYI, I am looking for a studio in the Manhattan area where we could record a podcast episode.
That would be awesome.
I think so. I think maybe my WeWork will have one, but I don't know for sure.
Did you watch that show on Apple TV about WeWork?
I did. That's pretty good. Some friends told me about a book where they discuss the Silicon Valley startup culture of the mid-2010s, and it's just interesting to see all this stuff play out.
How's Ellie? How's her summer vacation going?

Dude. So last week she did cheer camp, which was cute and fun and everything, but this week she is in Harry Potter camp. And they did something where they had, I think, Sprite, some sort of clear carbonated beverage-y thing, and they put some clear stuff in, and it reacts when you have the Sorting Hat on, and it sorts you into your house by color.
That's awesome. So where'd she get sorted?
Hers turned red. So just like every test she's ever done, she made it into Gryffindor.
Lucky her. She must be happy.
She was so excited.
Did she get to pick a wand too? Did they have different wands and everything?

They're going to go to Ollivander's this week. They're going to get to taste butterbeer. They're getting chocolate frogs, which she's excited about. I think when they do Ollivander's, it's chocolate Harry Potter wands. But they're learning defense tomorrow. She has Defense Against the Dark Arts class.
That's awesome. If she's into Harry Potter and stuff, you've got to get her down to Universal Studios, to the Harry Potter land.
We're reading Chamber of Secrets right now.
Oh, nice. Is this your first time going through the series?

Well, we're doing one a year, because they get progressively more complex and dark. You remember, last year we did Philosopher's Stone, and this year we're doing Chamber of Secrets. And those illustrated books are so amazing.
Oh yeah, I love those. They're perfect, especially for reading aloud with your children.
Yep. And by the time you guys get to the later ones… the first five are done, so far.
So yeah, we're only doing one a year, so we've got plenty of time.
By the time you get to the last one, HBO should be like two seasons into their show, probably.
Oh, you think it's going to take that long?
I assume, with the writers striking and stuff now, it probably won't even come out until '25.
Yeah. I'm just going to say this: if there are any writers listening, you're picking the wrong time in technology to try this game. AI is getting so stinking good.
Yeah. Supposedly Hollywood right now is using AI to write scripts and just wants to pay writers, when the strike ends, to come back and edit, essentially polish it up.

That's what I mean. You've got to think things through, y'all. AI wrote an excellent short story for me the other day, because there's this person at work who hoards vacation days like Scrooge hoards money. And people make fun of her for it, you know, because you can't carry over many of them into next year.
So I was like, AI, write me a Christmas carol, except instead of money, Diana is obsessed with vacation days and how it ruins her life.
And it turned out awesome. I was like, man, this is creepy, how good it's getting.
You and Ellie saw The Little Mermaid, right?
Oh, we did. Wasn't it good? It exceeded my expectations. I was blown away by it.

I've got to tell you one thing I was really surprised about. When we left, Christine was like, "I don't know, it was okay." And then she sat on it for a few days, and she's like, "I really liked that. That was pretty impressive." She wasn't immediately won over, but the more it settled with her… she wants to see it again already.

Yeah, I think it may be my favorite live-action remake so far. Sebastian and Scuttle were hilarious. Awkwafina knocked it out of the park. I just did not like the song, and I think 90% of it was the continual saying of "scuttlebutt." I just did not like it.
No, I don't think anyone liked that song.
You've heard it flopped in Asian countries, though, right?

Yep. A friend of mine who's Taiwanese and works with me was talking about how badly it's doing over there, because everybody grew up with the books and they want a white, red-headed Ariel, which I thought was interesting.
How did you feel about Javier Bardem as King Triton?
I actually liked him.

I found his performance lackluster. Stiff. He could have and should have done a lot more, compared to Melissa McCarthy as Ursula, right? But the big scene where I think he should have done more was the anger, wrecking her storage area. Because in the film, King Triton just had such a large presence. I remember as a kid, I was watching with my little sister, and she was as scared of his anger and wrath in that scene as she was of some of the Ursula stuff.

Yeah, that's a fair point. What I liked about this one is they changed the curse, so she didn't even remember she had to kiss Eric. So it was more than just "I have to kiss him." She actually had to fall for him too.
Well, and it made more sense, because in the other movie, all she had to do was kiss him. She could have just grabbed his face and kissed him.

Yeah. Oh, and the dog. If you have children and have not taken them to see it yet, I don't say this about a lot of movies, but this is a theater movie. This is one you will want to see in the full theater. The hundred-and-some-odd different sound channels make a difference. We saw it in IMAX, and it just blew us away, especially for scenes like "Under the Sea," which was awesome, and "Kiss the Girl," which is hilarious. They made it so funny. It wasn't just a shot-for-shot remake, which is how I felt Beauty and the Beast with Emma Watson was.
Yes, it was. It lacked any difference.
I think Disney's learning, after The Lion King. I think they're learning that if we're going to lean into this and do live-action movies, we've got to have a voice for these movies as well.
That's why I really liked Aladdin as well. They changed it enough.

I did like Aladdin a lot. I like this one more, though. And 100% of it is my expectation for the Genie. No matter how well Will Smith did, especially the longer I sit with it, it's just not Robin Williams' Genie.
Yeah. I do wonder, if he were alive, would they recast him to play it again? I don't even know.
Yeah. But the animation was so cool with that. I don't know if they could have done it justice with live action.
Yeah, that's true. But it's a definite watch. What else have you watched or done, Anthony? What have you been doing on your ridiculously long summer break from me?

Oh man, it has felt very long. Let's see. What have I been doing? Well, by the time this drops, I will have seen The Flash, which I'm excited about, and I will have seen The Blackening, which looks hilarious. Have you seen the trailer for that?
I have. I can't wait. That looks amazing.
I've binged the first two seasons of From, which, y'all, if you're not watching that show, you need to, because that show's incredible.
I cannot agree more. We have binged season one. I cannot get enough of it. There is nothing else I want to watch.
It's better than the early seasons of The Walking Dead to me.

I feel like it came out of nowhere too. It's an MGM Plus original and now all of a sudden I see loads of people talking about it. Just over the past week or two I see it's getting a lot of attention and I'm glad because I want it to continue but it's great. It is so, so, so good. Yeah, for those who haven't seen it, it's like, it's kind of like a mix between Lost and The Walking Dead. Like, you go into this town, but you can't leave. There was another show like this where people would come in, and Wayward Pines, that was it, not Falls. Wayward Pines. I do remember that show. I loved Wayward Pines, but this, the way they're doing this is so much better. Does it have, I know there's good and there's bad in this.
This could be taken good or bad, depending on who you are. But does this have a really good M. Night Shyamalan feel to you?

Like early, still-mysterious M. Night Shyamalan. It's everything I loved about The Village, because there's some mysterious… I don't want to give anything away. There's some mysterious evil force that's terrorizing the town, like in The Village. And like The Village, you don't see it or know what it is.
We don't actually see it attack. We don't see how it does the damage, and that, to me, is terrifying.
My favorite character on the show, though, is a guy who got stuck there who thought it was all a practical joke at first. A really rich guy who thought he was in a big escape room.
You didn't hate him?
I think he's hilarious.

Oh my gosh. Please cut this out. But he has so much Silicon Valley bro in him that I was just like, whatever these bad things are, if there is a God in this universe that we're watching, he will be eaten tonight.
I'll just say right now, if they are all dead in the end, I'm going to be annoyed.
Oh, but they have to go into some sort of weird church, and that doesn't explain why everything is all the things.
I'm still not over that ending. That's my fear with this writers' strike. Lost was damaged during a writers' strike.
Everything was at the time. Heroes lost. Didn't come back from it.

A lot of shows still recovered but those did not. They need to resolve this soon. They're not going to have... I think they have to resolve it soon. They're not going to have anything come September for the new seasons if they don't resolve this. Oh, they will.
You think they're going to go AI? I think they'll use AI and hire scabs. You don't think that the SAG will step in and also start striking with their actors?
Maybe.
I don't know. But one thing that will not be affected is what we're covering tonight. Well, I don't know. Is it canceled indefinitely?
I didn't think so. It could still happen.
So tonight, Thom and I are covering the three Christmas episodes of Cartoon Network Adult Swim's hit comedy Rick and Morty.
We made a terrible mistake.
Speak for yourself.
No, not forcing Julia to watch this and talk to us about it.

Oh, well, I was about to say, for a sneak peek behind the curtain: I actually have this on the calendar in a few weeks, and when I was talking to Thom about recording something, I was like, maybe you should do Rick and Morty while Julia's gone, and spare her.
I'd actually be curious to see what she would have thought.

I would too. But I think in the long run, she'll be happy she's not a part of this. So, Julia, if you're listening afterward, let us know what you think on all our social media. And if you don't, we'll be sure to ask you at our next recording what you think, on the spot, and not edit it out.

So, for those who don't know, the series follows the misadventures of Rick Sanchez, a cynical mad scientist, and his good-hearted but fretful grandson, Morty Smith, who split their time between domestic life and interdimensional adventures that take place across an infinite number of realities, often traveling to other planets and dimensions through portals and on Rick's flying saucer.

Yeah, the series started out as a parody, essentially a Back to the Future. And if you look at the character designs, they do look like Doc Brown and Marty McFly. 100% an old guy, crazy white hair, younger kid, but nerd. I do want to ask you, do you have any history with this show before tonight? Yes, of course I do.
Of course, I've seen Rick and Morty. Some of it I find funny. Some of it I don't. I'm not part of the cult following, but Rick and Morty's been there for me for those six years.

Yeah, I love Rick and Morty. It got funnier for me as it went along because they stopped with a lot. Well, it's still a lot of immature humor, but Rick doesn't burp every five seconds in later seasons. and they toned all that stuff down. All the food hanging and dribbling from his mouth all the time and the burps. Yeah, that got old. But I do, I really like this show. I think it's smart. I think it can be surprisingly emotional at times.
And it has a big mythology. I'm excited to see how it plays out in the end. It's an overarching story.
So I have a question for you, because I know you like Family Guy, I know you like Bob's Burgers. You're an adult-cartoon type of guy. Where does this fall in your adult cartoon ranking?

It depends. If we're talking early-to-mid Simpsons, it's well below that. Same thing with early Family Guy. Unlike a lot of the other stuff, you know, Family Guy's gone downhill, American Dad went downhill, I lost interest in a lot of those. Bob's Burgers is still okay. It's hit or miss. But like South Park, I agree with you, this has gotten better over time. The writing, the scripts, the storylines… I can't say matured, after what we watched today, but the characters have matured. Even Rick has become more palatable.
Yeah. For me, I would put this on top of my adult cartoons. I like this. Then Archer, and Family Guy.
I've never been into Archer.
Pretty good. That's ending soon.
Speaking of Bob's Burgers, you have the same actor.

Yep. So the creator of the show is somebody we have covered before. Dan Harmon also created Community, so we don't have to get into him. But the co-creator of the show is Justin Roiland, who has been accused of domestic violence and workplace harassment. Apparently all the charges were dropped due to lack of evidence, according to the courts, but he has still been fired from Rick and Morty going forward. So I'm curious to see how the show goes without him, because he is the voice of both Rick and Morty on this show, and a lot of the lesser-known characters.
Yep. Dan Harmon has been problematic too.

He has been. Did we cover that? Oh, with Community, I think we have, yeah. Okay. I don't want to get into that because that's really dark, but who would have thought that people who create a show this twisted would be problematic in real life? I feel like that's a trend when you go back through history. A lot of genius creators are very problematic when you look at them. It's sad, but I think you're right. It is sad. Yeah, I feel like we should say here at the top, by the way, listeners, this is a pretty adult show. So if you're listening with kids, you may want to wait till kids are out of the room. There's no way to avoid some of the adult stuff that would be talked about on this show. So there's your warning.

But yeah, Justin Roiland plays two main characters, Rick Sanchez and Morty Smith. Chris Parnell plays Jerry Smith, Morty's pathetic father and son-in-law. It seems to be a trend for him because he plays a pathetic Cyril on Archer.

We may have covered him. I don't know if he was in any of the Christmas episodes of 30 Rock, but he was Dr. Leo Spaceman on 30 Rock. He was on SNL for a few years. He plays Doug on Family Guy. He did The Simpsons. He's done a lot of voice acting.
Yeah, I like this guy.
He was on Kimmy Schmidt. He was a voice on Curious George. He had an appearance on Will & Grace. He's done a lot. And then, of course, he was Thomas Edison and Carl Sagan on Drunk History.
We may have covered him in Black-ish.
Oh yeah. He's the dean.
Oh, right, right, right.

So it's possible. But he's good. I like this guy. Playing Beth Smith, his wife, and Space Beth, the clone of his wife, is Sarah Chalke. People will know her best as Becky Conner in Roseanne, and Elliot Reid in Scrubs.
That's where I think she had a bigger impact. She was also in Firefly Lane, How You Met Your Mother, Estella, and in Cougar Town. She was also on some Netflix show called Dogs in Space.
She was on Grey's Anatomy, Robot Chicken.

She was the voice in Prep and Landing, Naughty Burst Nice. she was the elf, right? The girl elf. We covered her. And then the last main cast member here is Spencer Grammer, who voices Summer, Morty's older sister. This is her biggest show, but she was also Casey Cartwright on ABC Family's Creek.

If y'all remember that. But she has guest starred on stuff like Grey's Anatomy, Chicago PD, Robot Chicken. Law and Order, of course. Law and Order. Cheers in 92. too, where she was playing Little Girl.

So, yeah, that's our main cast. We do have some big guest stars in each of these episodes, which we'll talk about. We do. Including this first episode, which is season one, episode three, Anatomy Park, which is a spoof on Jurassic Park. Oh my gosh. let's jump right in, because I love this episode. Not to give it away, but It's something, man. It is something. We start on Christmas morning and of course, as is common in many families nowadays, the whole family is on their iPhones or iPads. They're not having any human connection. And Jerry is like he just wants to have a human holiday especially with his parents visiting, coming to visit. So he collects all the electronics and stocking and, you know, says we're all going to spend some time together today. Rick, meanwhile, shows up with a homeless guy in a Santa outfit named Ruben. Ruben.
They're going to the garage, and he brings Morty into the garage. And apparently Ruben has been a test subject for Rick for many years.
I was going to say, Ruben is played by Jess Harnell. Do you know Jess Harnell?
Who is that?
Jess Harnell's the voice of Crash Bandicoot.
Oh, okay.
And he's the voice of Darth Maul in the Star Wars video games.
Ah, okay. Very cool.
And some other stuff. He's Ironhide in Transformers. He played a few presidents, and in Mr. Peabody & Sherman.
Yeah. So Ruben, though, is ground zero for one of Rick's inventions. He created a theme park inside this body called Anatomy Park.
Isn't there a little controversy over whose idea it actually was, though, between Rick and Dr. Xenon Bloom, played by John Oliver?

Who was a genius. Yeah, there is a little controversy. Rick fully takes credit, though, for Pirates of the Pancreas, which he feels is an undervalued idea, even though Xenon Bloom and the rest of the staff of this park are like, it doesn't make sense to have a ride called Pirates of the Pancreas.

Essentially, Ruben is dying due to alcoholism, his liver shutting down, and as such, there is a problem with Anatomy Park. Like Jurassic Park, the systems are shut down, and the body is attacking itself. So Rick shrinks Morty and injects him into Ruben, where Morty must team up with Dr. Xenon Bloom and a few other park employees, who are parodies of people from Predator and movies like that. You have Poncho, the big muscle guy with the gun, and you have Annie, the hot blonde, who Morty immediately develops a crush on.
You have a guy who's basically Goofy from Disney, not allowed to take off his hat.
Yep. So while this is going on, Jerry's parents arrive for Christmas, but they do not arrive alone. They arrive with a friend. What's the friend's name?
Jacob.

Named Jacob. Yep. So Jerry's parents are this older white couple, and Jacob is this younger Black man, and it soon becomes clear that the three of them have some sexual arrangement, basically a cuckolding scenario, much to Jerry's disturbance. And he becomes even more disturbed when everyone else in the family just accepts it. They're all okay with it.
Cherry's dad tries to normalize it like, Son, it's okay. They let me watch all the time. Sometimes in the closet. All the time in a Superman outfit.
So weird, man.
In Ruben's body, meanwhile, Ruben dies. Which unleashes bacteria and viruses throughout Anatomy Park. Well, it's gone rogue.
They featured all of these... It's supposed to be all the viruses and bacteria that have fought humanity for years, but they say they've escaped. Yeah, so we have gonorrhea and buponic plague.
E. coli is actually shaped like a virus, not a bacteria. Just saying.

And they start picking off the crew of Anatomy Park one by one. But we find out about a double cross: Poncho compromised the safety of Anatomy Park. He is basically the Wayne Knight character from Jurassic Park. He was stealing the viruses to sell them to the highest bidder, but instead of the bubonic plague, he wanted to sell it to North Korea, Iran, Russia, all of America's enemies.
Anything would be better than working for Dr. Xenon Bloom.
But of course, Poncho falls to his death fighting off the bubonic plague when he gets out.

Rick, meanwhile, is doing everything he can to keep Ruben's body somewhat functioning, somewhat so that he can find a way to get Morty and the crew of an enemy park out. otherwise they'll die inside of it. So they finally decide that they need to go out through the nipple. Yes, which they decide when they're watching a video, again, from Jurassic Park with the ride they're on where Dr. Hammond's explaining the cloning of the dinosaurs' process. This is an animatronic Ruben explaining the human body to them. And Morty's making out with Annie, and it's one of my favorite quotes in the episode. Rick is like, Morty, can you get to the nipple? And he's like, oh jeez, Rick. I hope I get more than that.
So they head to the nipple.
On their way, they have to go through the small intestine.
They have to go through the small intestine. Which is just the head. And to get through it, you go to the left, then to the right, then to the left, then to the right, then to the left.
Well, I like that they have to escape on a monorail, and somebody has to stay behind to run the monorail.
Wait, before that, we missed the song. "It's a Small Intestine."
It is. I don't have the lyrics. It's basically "It's a Small World," but about a small intestine.

Yep, yep. It's funny. But yeah, like you said, they have to get to a monorail, but it's not autopiloted. So Xenon Bloom stays behind to let Morty and Annie escape. And the minute it starts taking off, he's like, "Son of a bitch, it is autopiloted! Wait for me!"
He gets attacked by the boobotic plague and dies.
Meanwhile, while they're heading to the nipple to escape out the nipple hole, Rick blows up Ruben, so when they come out of the nipple, they'll come out fully sized.
He enlarges him.

Enlarges. And he has to take him to space to do that. This is one of my favorite parts, because Ruben's naked body is hovering over planet Earth, and the news is commenting on it. They're like, "Well, it's a giant head over so-and-so. One can only imagine what the people of Montana must be seeing." And you see this lumberjack alone in the woods as the shadow of Ruben's penis overcomes the woods, and the lumberjack just looks up and starts shaking, wide-eyed.

They had his eyes over New York, and they go to California, and they're talking about how large his feet are, even in proportion to his body. "And you know what they say about people with large feet." And then we cut to the lumberjack. It was amazing.

So they come out of the nipple, full-sized, and Rick is there to get them in his flying saucer, and Ruben explodes, and blood rain starts falling everywhere, all over America. And on the TV, they're telling everyone this is fine.

Well, it's funny, because before Morty and Annie escape, they are attacked by hepatitis A. And again, it's a spoof of the closing scene of Jurassic Park, with the raptors. Before they can be eaten by hepatitis A, hepatitis C, a much larger virus, comes in and attacks hepatitis A, just like the T. rex did in Jurassic Park. And Morty even comments, "I don't get it. Did we have a relationship with that guy? Why is he saving us?"

Well, Rick, Morty, and Annie come back to the house where Jerry has kind of learned to accept Jacob because he saw the way, So Ethan, who is Summer's boyfriend, came to the house upset with Summer because she hasn't been texting him back because Jerry took away all the electronics. And Jacob helps Ethan confess all his anger. And Jerry had a newfound respect for that. So back at the house.
Rick's upset and Anatomy Park is destroyed.

And Annie says, well, I studied Dr. Xenon Bloom's work. So I have the knowledge to build new ones. So Rick shrinks her back down and leaves Morty depressed. And he injects her into, eventually injects her into Ethan, who wears them. They're going to build a new anatomy park. And then she goes in, she tells him I've studied Dr. Bloom's work for years. I know everything and I've got ideas on how to make it better. And he's, and Rick asks, what do you think about pirates of the pancreas? And she just builds him up. If this is a great idea. Then in an after-credits scene on a conference call with the new Anatomy Park staff, Annie says the crew reveals plans to scrap Rick's Pirates of the Pagrius, and Rick gets upset and hangs up on her.
And he's no longer interested. So, this episode was funny.
Hilarious. It's set at Christmas. Christmas is not integral. It's not a Christmas episode.
It was more integral to the family stuff.

It was, but that was also a really small part. It does have a Linus moment, when Jerry realizes his parents' relationship, while unconventional, works for them, and accepts this third into their family.

Rick did have a quote at the beginning of this about Christmas. He says, "Oh, what have we got here? A bunch of people with their faces stuffed in computers. Don't you realize that Christ was born today? Don't you realize that Christ, our Savior, was born today? What kind of Christmas is this?"
I like how the news announcers constantly refer to Ruben, too, as the giant naked sky Santa.
I like Jerry singing at the beginning of the episode. I wanted the lyrics, so I actually went and found the script, where he's just butchering "Last Christmas."

I also loved when Anatomy Park was failing inside of Ruben, and Rick didn't know if he could get them out. He tells Morty, "Listen, if the situation in there keeps on darkening, you've got to do yourself a favor and pop by Pirates of the Pancreas. I mean, the top priority is get out of there, guys. But if that proves impossible, you've got to treat yourself. It's really good, Morty."
I like the way Jerry gets the kids to put their phones in the stocking.
He threatens Summer by telling her he's going to join Facebook if she doesn't put her phone in.
Let's be honest, if our parents had thought about it, they could have gotten a lot out of us years ago by threatening to join Facebook.

I did like the Phil Collins reference. To deflect from the fact that he just brought a homeless Santa into the house, who's supposedly been a friend of his and just keeps talking about really old war stuff, Pearl Harbor, Korea, randomly, Rick says, "Don't worry about your Christmas, Jerry. I'll be with Ruben in my workshop while you guys are having another day in Phil Collins' proverbial paradise." Referencing "Another Day in Paradise," where Phil Collins sings about people ignoring homeless people.
But yeah. So, like you said, set at Christmas, had somewhat of a Linus moment. What would you give this one?
It was funny, but I'm coming in at a five, for lack of Christmas-iness overall.
Yeah. So for the record, this is one of my favorite Rick and Morty episodes. I love this one. But due to lack of Christmas, I'd have to give it a six.
So five and a half. So, Thom, do you want to walk us through our next episode?

Not really. I did not love this one as much. This next one is season four, episode five, "Rattlestar Ricklactica." All right. So in this episode, we are back at Christmas, and for some weird reason, Morty has killed a space snake and feels bad, and he wants to work hard to make up for it, right?
Yeah. Well, it's important to say that he killed a space snake when Rick's car gets a flat tire in space, and Rick warns him, "Stay in the car."

And Morty does not and gets bit. He gets out of the spaceship and in this spaceship, Rick says he gets a flat tire and Morty's like, how does a spaceship get a, how do you get a flat tire in space? And he's like, something sharp, obviously. And then the car, it's vibrating and Morty's confused. And Rick's like, I put it in a flat car simulator. Then he turns it off. And yes, the big deal here is Rick tells Morty not to get out of the spaceship, not to get out of the car. He does. He gets bitten. They have to go back to the snake planet so that Rick can create an anti-venom. And I don't understand what I watched. I'm going to be honest. We somehow get into time travel. We're in a Terminator scenario.

Basically, on the snake planet, they have like 19 billion snakes. Snakes divided into 10,000 nations based on race, which Rick remarks the concept of racing snakes is hilarious to him. Yeah, he's like, oh, I hate you because you're a different colored snake than me.

But Morty is horrified they killed the astronaut who might have been the snake's last one for survival. Like, he even cries out, 19 billion snakes lost all hope because of me, Rick. Rick says it's not your fault, it's the snakes. And they were the, he was the idiot who bit for salient contact. So they go home and Morty keeps the snake and has a vigil for it. And he comes up with this idea, essentially, to restore hope to the snakes by going to a pet store, buying a lookalike, and sending it back. Sending it back. We then get a montage of the snake culture, the scientists, the politicians, the military attempting to interact with the snake they don't understand.

And the snake, essentially, it alters the entire course of history for these snakes. As a result, in the future, they end up creating robot snakes, and there's this big uprising. Again, very Terminator-esque. The snakes end up developing time travel, they go back in time, and they end up on Earth. The surviving snakes somehow win the war because Morty helped them unite. Morty was their flag. Morty with a snake wrapped around him became their flag. He was their hero.
But when they, in order to end this,

Rick's big thought is, "You know what? We just need to introduce time travel earlier to these snakes." So he's really ticked that he has to learn snake math so that he can explain time travel to snakes. He creates a book, and they go back to 1985 and leave the book.
Did you notice that at Snake MIT, the snake was wearing a shirt with an Apple logo with a bite taken out of it?

Yep. And so these snakes end up developing time travel. One of the snakes boldly goes back in time, goes to the snake Ford's Theatre, and gives Abraham Lincoln a note that just says "S's." Abraham Lincoln ducks, and then they all beat the crap out of snake John Wilkes Booth. Then the next one goes to 1938 to stop snake Adolf Hitler.
